title: English: Grammar and Punctuation (B1)
source: Written for Kru, Nov 24 (Henry): 100 questions on grammar, punctuation and writing skills. American English.

questions.q: I ___ to Phuket three times.
questions.why: An experience up to now (three times): present perfect.

questions.q: She ___ in Chiang Mai in 2019.
questions.why: 'In 2019' is a finished time, so we use the past simple.

questions.q: Have you ___ your homework yet?
I haven't seen him ___ Monday.
We ___ dinner already, so we're not hungry.
When ___ you last see her?
questions.why: 'When' asks about a finished time, so we use the past simple.

questions.q: She has worked here ___ ten years.
Look! Somebody ___ my bike!
questions.why: We can see the result now, so we use the present perfect.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: I saw that movie last night.
I have seen that movie last night.
I see that movie last night.
I have saw that movie last night.
questions.why: With 'last night' (a finished time) we use the past simple.

questions.q: She is tired because she ___ for two hours.
questions.why: A longer activity up to now with a visible result: present perfect continuous.

questions.q: I ___ Japan twice.
questions.why: Experience up to now: present perfect.

questions.q: She ___ to Paris in 2019.
We ___ lunch yet.
He ___ his keys. He can't get in.
Did you ___ the movie last night?
I ___ here since 2015.
They ___ married for ten years.
___ you ever eaten durian?
When ___ you buy that phone?
questions.why: "When" asks about a finished time: past simple.

questions.q: I ___ my homework already.
She ___ the book last week.
He has worked here ___ three years.
He has worked here ___ 2021.
My brother ___ in a hospital for five years now.
How long ___ you known her?
We ___ to the beach yesterday.
Look! It ___ snowing! It's amazing.
I ___ never ___ a snake.
She ___ just ___ home.
Which sentence is correct?
choices: I have seen him an hour ago.
I see him an hour ago.
I saw him an hour ago.
I was seeing him an hour ago.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
At 8 p.m. last night, I ___ TV.
questions.why: An action in progress at a time in the past: past continuous.

questions.q: They ___ soccer when it started to rain.
questions.why: A longer action in progress: past continuous.

questions.q: What ___ you doing at 10 o'clock?
I was walking home when I ___ my friend.
questions.why: The short action that interrupts uses the past simple.

questions.q: The phone rang while she ___ a shower.
questions.why: 'While' + past continuous for the longer action.

questions.q: When we arrived at the movie theater, the movie ___.
questions.why: The movie started BEFORE we arrived: past perfect.

questions.q: She ___ the book before she saw the movie.
questions.why: Past perfect for the earlier action.

questions.q: I was tired because I ___ all night.
questions.why: Past perfect shows the earlier reason.

questions.q: By the time he called, I ___ home.
questions.why: 'By the time' + past simple: the earlier action uses past perfect.

questions.q: I ___ for an hour when the bus finally came.
questions.why: A longer action before another past action: past perfect continuous.

questions.q: When I arrived, the movie ___.
She was tired because she ___ all night.
questions.why: Reason that happened first: past perfect.

questions.q: By the time we got there, the bus ___.
I ___ dinner when the lights went out.
They ___ to the movie theater before they ate.
He ___ his homework before his mom came home.
While I ___ the dishes, he was watching TV.
questions.why: Two actions at the same time: past continuous.

questions.q: She told me she ___ the book before.
We ___ for an hour when it started to rain.
questions.why: Longer action before another: past perfect continuous.

questions.q: I realized I ___ my wallet at home.
questions.why: The leaving happened before the realizing.

questions.q: Mom ___ in the kitchen when I came in.
questions.why: She was in the middle of cooking.

questions.q: He ___ never ___ sushi before that day.
When the teacher came in, the students ___.
After she ___ breakfast, she went to school.
He ___ asleep when the phone rang.
It ___ all morning, so the ground was wet.
questions.why: Past perfect continuous gives the cause.

questions.q: Which is correct?
choices: I have already eaten when he called.
I already eat when he called.
I had already eaten when he called.
I was already eat when he called.
questions.why: Past perfect for the earlier action.

questions.q: Which is correct?
We ___ the room before the guests arrived.
She ___ when she saw the accident.
I didn't know that he ___ married.
I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.why: We can see the evidence now: be going to.

questions.q: We ___ my cousin on Sunday. It's arranged.
I'm thirsty. I ___ get some water.
questions.why: A decision made at the moment of speaking: will.

questions.q: She ___ study medicine. She has already applied.
questions.why: A plan made before now: be going to.

questions.q: The train ___ at 6:15 tomorrow.
Don't worry. I ___ help you.
This time next week I ___ on a beach.
questions.why: An action in progress at a future time: future continuous.

questions.q: I'll call you when I ___ home.
questions.why: After 'when' we use the present simple for the future.

questions.q: By 2030, scientists ___ a cure.
questions.why: 'By' + a future time: future perfect (will have + past participle).

questions.q: Look at the sky! It ___ rain.
questions.why: A prediction from what we see.

questions.q: I ___ my grandma this weekend. I've bought the ticket.
"I'm cold." "I ___ close the window."
The train ___ at 9:15 tomorrow.
She ___ be a doctor when she grows up.
questions.why: A future plan: be going to.

questions.q: I think it ___ be hot tomorrow.
We ___ meet at 6. Is that OK?
I promise I ___ tell anyone.
By next year, I ___ English for ten years.
This time tomorrow, I ___ on a beach.
What ___ you do tonight?
He ___ his driver's license next month. He has an exam on Monday.
Perhaps it ___ rain later.
Be careful! You ___ fall!
When I ___ home, I will call you.
We will go out if it ___ raining.
I ___ the exam tomorrow, but I don't feel ready.
"Who wants to help?" "I ___!"
The meeting ___ at 3 p.m. on Friday.
She says she ___ the cake tomorrow.
Which sentence is correct?
choices: We're going to visit Chiang Mai.
We going to visit Chiang Mai.
We are go to visit Chiang Mai.

questions.q: If you heat ice, it ___.
questions.why: A general truth: zero conditional (present + present).

questions.q: If it rains, we ___ at home.
questions.why: A real possibility: first conditional (present + will).

questions.q: If I ___ rich, I would buy a boat.
questions.why: An unreal situation: second conditional (past + would). 'Were' is used for all persons.

questions.q: If you study, you ___ the test.
questions.why: First conditional: if + present, will + base verb.

questions.q: If I had more time, I ___ learn French.
questions.why: Second conditional: if + past, would + base verb.

questions.q: What would you do if you ___ a million dollars?
questions.why: Second conditional: the 'if' part uses the past simple.

questions.q: If she ___ hungry, she can eat now.
questions.why: A real situation: if + present simple.

questions.q: I won't go out ___ it stops raining.
If I were you, I ___ apologize.
questions.why: Advice with 'If I were you' uses would.

questions.q: She would be happier if she ___ more friends.
questions.why: Second conditional: the 'if' part uses the past simple.

questions.q: If it rains, we ___ stay at home.
If I ___ more money, I would buy a car.
If she ___ harder, she would pass the test.
What ___ you do if you saw a ghost?
If he ___ up early, he will catch the bus.
Unless you ___ now, you'll be late.
If I ___ the answer, I would tell you.
If it ___ tomorrow, we'll go to the beach.
If we hurry, we ___ the train.
If I ___ a bird, I would fly to you.
If you press this button, the machine ___.
If I had known, I ___ you.
If you don't wear a coat, you ___ cold.
What would happen if everyone ___ the same?
She'd be rich if she ___ that job.
If you ___ something, tell me.
I will help you if you ___ me.
If I won the lottery, I ___ travel the world.
Which sentence is correct?
choices: If it will rain, I'll stay home.
If it rained, I'll stay home.
If it rains, I stay home will.
If it rains, I'll stay home.

questions.q: If I ___ free tomorrow, I'll call you.
You ___ drive without a license.
You ___ wear a uniform at my school. It's a rule.
questions.why: 'Have to' shows a rule or duty.

questions.q: ___ I open the window?
questions.why: We ask for permission with 'Can I...?'.

questions.q: I ___ speak French when I was five.
questions.why: 'Could' is the past of 'can' for ability.

questions.q: It's cold. You ___ take a coat.
He ___ be tired. He worked all night.
questions.why: 'Must' shows that we are almost sure.

questions.q: I'm not sure, but she ___ be at the library.
You ___ come to the meeting. It's not necessary.
questions.why: 'Don't have to' means it is not necessary.

questions.q: I ___ go to the dentist yesterday.
questions.why: The past of 'have to' is 'had to'.

questions.q: She ___ be at work. I saw her in the park a minute ago.
questions.why: 'Can't' shows that we are sure something is not true.

questions.q: You ___ wear a seat belt. It's the law.
She ___ be at home. The lights are on.
He ___ be a doctor. He's only ten!
You ___ eat so much sugar. It's bad for you.
We ___ have a test tomorrow, but I'm not sure.
___ you help me with this bag, please?
I ___ run fast when I was young.
You ___ pay now. You can pay later.
You ___ smoke here. It's forbidden.
___ I come in?
She ___ speak Japanese. She lived in Tokyo for 5 years.
You ___ see a dentist. Your tooth hurts.
It ___ rain later. Take an umbrella.
We ___ leave now, or we'll miss the bus.
I ___ rather stay at home tonight.
You ___ have told me earlier!
He ___ be tired. He's been working all day.
___ I open the window? It's hot in here.
You ___ to study harder.
I ___ finished my work yesterday. I'm sorry.
The door is locked. They ___ be home.
English ___ in many countries.
questions.why: Present simple passive: is/are + past participle.

questions.q: The window ___ by a ball yesterday.
questions.why: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle.

questions.q: These cars ___ in Japan.
questions.why: Present simple passive with a plural subject: are made.

questions.q: The letter ___ last week.
My phone ___ at the moment.
questions.why: Present continuous passive: is being + past participle.

questions.q: Which sentence is the passive of 'They built the bridge in 1990'?
The homework ___ yet.
questions.why: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle.

questions.q: The thief ___ by the police last night.
questions.why: Past simple passive of 'catch': was caught.

questions.q: Who ___ the Mona Lisa?
questions.why: 'Who' is the subject, so the verb is active.

questions.q: The new rules ___ to all students next week.
questions.why: Future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.q: English ___ all over the world.
The window ___ by the boy yesterday.
This cake ___ by my mom.
The room ___ every day.
A lot of rice ___ in Thailand.
The Eiffel Tower ___ in 1889.
My bike ___ last week.
The letters ___ by the mail carrier every morning.
The homework ___ by tomorrow.
questions.why: Modal passive: must be + past participle.

Which sentence is passive?
Which is correct?
The Mona Lisa ___ by Leonardo da Vinci.
The girl ___ is sitting there is my sister.
This is the book ___ I told you about.
That's the shop ___ I bought my shoes.
A man ___ car was stolen called the police.
I know a restaurant ___ serves great pizza.
The people ___ live next door are friendly.
Bangkok, ___ is the capital of Thailand, is very big.
questions.why: Extra information between commas uses 'which', not 'that'.

questions.q: Is this the pen ___ you were looking for?
The teacher ___ I met yesterday is from Canada.
questions.why: 'Who' refers to a person (the object of 'met').

questions.q: The city ___ I was born is very small.
The man ___ lives next door is a pilot.
This is the book ___ I told you about.
She is the girl ___ bag was stolen.
I like people ___ make me laugh.
The movie ___ we saw was funny.
My friend, ___ lives in Chiang Mai, called me.
questions.why: Extra info about a person: who.

questions.q: Bangkok, ___ is the capital, is huge.
questions.why: Extra info about a thing: which.

questions.q: The day ___ we met was rainy.
This is the reason ___ I am late.
The woman ___ car is red is my aunt.
The teacher ___ taught us last year is very kind.
This is the house ___ I was born.
Is this the bag ___ you lost?
Everything ___ she said was true.
A person ___ cooks is called a cook.
The boy ___ I sat next to was friendly.
Tom, ___ brother is a singer, is my classmate.
Which sentence is correct?
choices: The pen that I lost was new.
The pen who I lost was new.
The pen whose I lost was new.
The pen where I lost was new.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: The students which study hard pass.
The students who study hard pass.
The students whose study hard pass.
The students where study hard pass.

questions.q: The man ___ I met yesterday is a teacher.
I enjoy ___ to music.
She wants ___ a doctor.
questions.why: After 'want' we use to + base verb.

questions.q: He is good at ___ chess.
questions.why: After a preposition we use the -ing form.

questions.q: We decided ___ a taxi.
questions.why: After 'decide' we use to + base verb.

questions.q: She suggested ___ to the beach.
I'm looking forward to ___ you.
questions.why: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so we use -ing.

questions.q: My parents let me ___ out late.
questions.why: After 'let' we use the base verb.

questions.q: He stopped ___ because he was tired.
Remember ___ the door when you leave.
questions.why: 'Remember to' = do not forget to do it.

questions.q: I'm used to ___ up early.
questions.why: 'Be used to' + -ing means something is normal for you.

Which is a complete sentence?
questions.why: A complete sentence has a subject and a verb and makes sense by itself.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.why: In American English the comma goes inside the quotation marks.

questions.q: Which sentence has the correct end punctuation?
questions.why: An exclamation ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.q: Which is a run-on sentence?
choices: I was tired, so I went to bed.
I was tired. I went to bed.
I was tired I went to bed.
I was tired because I worked.
questions.why: Two complete sentences are joined with no punctuation or linking word.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.why: Put a comma after 'However' at the start of a sentence.

questions.q: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
choices: I need three things: a pen, a book, and paper.
I need: three things a pen, a book, and paper.
I need three: things a pen, a book, and paper.
I: need three things a pen, a book, and paper.
questions.why: Use a colon after a complete sentence to introduce a list.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: My brother who lives in Phuket, is a chef.
My brother, who lives in Phuket is a chef.
My brother, who lives in Phuket, is a chef.
My brother who, lives in Phuket is a chef.
questions.why: Extra information goes between two commas.

questions.q: Which is a sentence fragment?
choices: I got home when it rained.
questions.why: 'When I got home' cannot stand alone: it needs a main clause.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: Although it was raining we went out.
Although it was raining, we went out.
Although, it was raining we went out.
Although it was raining. We went out.
questions.why: Put a comma after an introductory clause.

questions.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
choices: She loves reading, he prefers movies.
She loves reading; and he prefers movies.
She loves reading; he prefers movies.
She loves; reading he prefers movies.
questions.why: A semicolon joins two closely related complete sentences.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: I bought, apples bananas and milk.
I bought apples, bananas, and milk.
I bought apples bananas, and, milk.
I bought apples, bananas and, milk.
questions.why: Commas separate items in a list.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Although it was raining we played, outside.
Although it was raining, we played outside.
Although, it was raining we played outside.
Although it was raining. We played outside.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: My brother who is ten, loves games.
My brother, who is ten loves games.
My, brother who is ten, loves games.
My brother, who is ten, loves games.

questions.q: Which is a complete sentence?
questions.why: A complete sentence has a subject and a verb.

questions.q: Which is a fragment (not a complete sentence)?
Which sentence is correct?

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: I like tea; and my sister likes coffee.
I like tea, my sister likes coffee.
I like tea; my sister likes coffee.
I like tea. my sister likes coffee.
questions.why: A semicolon joins two related sentences.

questions.q: Which sentence has a run-on mistake?
choices: I was tired, so I went to bed.
I was tired. I went to bed.
I was tired, I went to bed.
I was tired; I went to bed.
questions.why: A comma alone cannot join two sentences.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.why: The question mark is inside the quotes.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: The childrens toys are on the floor.
The childrens' toys are on the floor.
The children toy's are on the floor.
The children's toys are on the floor.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
Which sentence is correct?

choices: We can go by bus, or, by train.
We can go by bus or by train.

questions.q: I was very tired, ___ I finished my homework.
She is tall ___ her brother is short.
Which word means the opposite of 'happy'?
questions.why: Sad is the opposite of happy.

questions.q: ___ the rain, we played outside.
___ he was tired, he kept working.
questions.why: 'Although' is followed by a clause (subject + verb).

questions.q: He didn't come ___ he was sick.

Her ___ in math is amazing.
Read: 'Nok loves animals, but she can't have a pet because her apartment doesn't allow them. Instead, she volunteers at an animal shelter on weekends.' Why can't Nok have a pet?
questions.why: The text says her apartment doesn't allow them.
